# Firmware Upload Skill

**Purpose:** Compile and upload the ESP32 bridge firmware over USB serial.

**When to use:** 
- Uploading code changes to the ESP32-S3
- Checking if the board is visible on the expected COM port
- Testing firmware compilation without uploading

## Quick Start

```powershell
.venv\Scripts\python.exe skills/firmware-upload/upload_firmware.py
```

## Common Operations

| Task | Command |
|---|---|
| **Compile + Upload** | `.venv\Scripts\python.exe skills/firmware-upload/upload_firmware.py` |
| **Compile only** | `.venv\Scripts\python.exe skills/firmware-upload/upload_firmware.py --skip-upload` |
| **Upload only (reuse build)** | `.venv\Scripts\python.exe skills/firmware-upload/upload_firmware.py --skip-compile` |
| **Specify COM port** | `.venv\Scripts\python.exe skills/firmware-upload/upload_firmware.py --port COM5` |

## Prerequisites

- Arduino IDE with `arduino-cli` in standard location
- ESP32 board package installed (`esp32:esp32`)
- USB cable connected from PC to ESP32-S3
- Run from repository root: `c:\git\MastervoltBridge`

## Troubleshooting

| Problem | Solution |
|---|---|
| "NOT FOUND" / no ports visible | Check USB cable, driver in Device Manager (look for "CP210x" or "USB Serial Device") |
| Wrong port detected | Script lists available ports; re-run with `--port COMx` |
| Compilation error | Fix the firmware error, re-run the script |

## Output

- Compilation logs and error messages
- Upload progress and confirmation
- Flash verification

Success: "✅ Upload complete" message and firmware version visible in `/api/device`
